goal: Correlate the approved change and the observed behavior, then restore the relay’s management boundary.
context: Builds on reading event logs and checking remote management from known client addresses. All records and probes are supplied for the virtual network.

concepts.title: Separate risk, weakness and evidence
concepts.text: A threat is something that could harm the network. A vulnerability is a weakness that could make that possible. An exploit uses a weakness to cause an unauthorized result. Here the broadened management rule is the weakness. The journal and virtual client probes show what was observed.

concepts.title: Follow the same device and time
concepts.text: Compare the approved revision, the revision that was applied and a later probe on the affected relay. A probe that reaches the sign-in boundary does not establish that the client successfully signed in. Look for a separate sign-in record for that client.

concepts.title: Check that the mitigation preserves real work
concepts.text: Restore the approved access boundary. Verify that approved systems still reach the sign-in prompt. Check the restricted clients as well. A broad permit and a blanket block both fail part of the job.

worked.label: Compare two records
worked.value:
West relay · Approved 17
West relay · Applied 19
worked.explanation: Both records concern the same device. The second revision differs from the ticket.

worked.label: Distinguish two observations
worked.value:
Guest trial · sign-in boundary reachable
Successful guest sign-in · no supplied record
worked.explanation: The practice probe shows broader access. The supplied record does not establish a successful sign-in for the guest.

worked.label: Verify the boundary after mitigation
worked.value:
Operations → allowed to attempt sign-in
Guest → denied before sign-in
worked.explanation: Check both the continued approved access and the restored restriction.

practice.title: Read the training relay journal
practice.action: Compare record 102 (approved revision), 104 (applied revision) and 106 (shared-desk observation). Look for other sign-in evidence on the same device.
practice.observe: Record 107 contains a successful sign-in for the shared desk. The unrelated aggregation note belongs to another device.

practice.title: Complete the evidence report
practice.action: Choose the approval, applied and post-change evidence records, then answer whether the restricted client has a separate successful sign-in record.
practice.observe: Your report should distinguish the client that reached the sign-in boundary and the independent sign-in observation.

practice.title: Restore and test the management boundary
practice.action: In the policy editor, allow only the two approved addresses, 192.0.2.53 and 192.0.2.54, in standard list 21. Keep SSH v2 and the incoming list. Apply and select Check workspace.
practice.observe: The two approved clients keep their access. The shared desk and visitor no longer reach sign-in.

requirements: Use the affected relay’s journal to identify the approved revision, applied revision and post-change restricted-client observation.
Record whether the supplied journal establishes a successful sign-in for the same restricted client.
Restore access only for the two approved systems and verify the four supplied client trials.

goal: Set a virtual facility policy that keeps necessary work possible while limiting and recording access to the network room.
context: Builds on tying a safeguard to evidence. This unit supplies work roles, approved times and visitor conditions.

concepts.title: Give people the access their role needs
concepts.text: Assign permissions for routine work and on-call faults separately. Restrict when maintenance can happen. A full block can stop needed work, while broadly available access exposes the room.

concepts.title: Require and verify an escort
concepts.text: Registration identifies a visitor in the supplied profile. In the default policy for the example, a visit also needs a present escort and a staffed time window. Check a legitimate visit as well as the failed case.

concepts.title: Give people a clear reporting route
concepts.text: An awareness procedure tells staff how to report an unexpected access request. Configure the destination, then inspect whether the supplied report reaches the security desk. Record denied access events for review.

worked.label: Define two permissions
worked.value:
Network operator · Any window
Visitor · Staffed with escort
worked.explanation: The operator can respond to the supplied fault. A visitor needs a registered identity and an escort at a staffed time.

worked.label: Verify different outcomes
worked.value:
Escorted visit · Allowed
Unescorted visit · Denied
worked.explanation: Compare a normal visit and a denied attempt. The permitted visit should still work.

worked.label: Route and retain evidence
worked.value:
Denied entries · recorded
Report destination · Security desk
worked.explanation: The reviewer gets the supplied event record and the staff report.

practice.title: Set the operator and technician windows
practice.action: Allow the workshop operator and facilities technician during staffed hours. Read the operator after-hours case as well.
practice.observe: This session does not require after-hours operator access.

practice.title: Require a present escort
practice.action: Set visitor access to Staffed with escort. Compare the escorted, unescorted and unverified visitor trials.
practice.observe: Only the escorted, registered visit during the staffed window is allowed.

practice.title: Retain and route evidence
practice.action: Record denied events and route the supplied suspicious-contact report to the security desk. Select Check workspace. Try a blanket visitor denial, review the allowed visit, then restore the working settings.
practice.observe: The expected event records are present. Denying every visit breaks the legitimate trial.

requirements: Keep on-call operator access for the supplied after-hours fault.
Allow technician access during staffed hours and allow a registered visitor only with an escort during staffed hours.
Keep the denied-event records and route the supplied staff report to the security desk.
